input.description: An `N+1` dimensional potentially ragged integer tensor with shape `[D1...DN, num_chars]`.

output_encoding.description: Unicode encoding that should be used to encode each code point sequence. Can be `"UTF-8"`, `"UTF-16-BE"`, or `"UTF-32-BE"`.

errors.description: Specifies the response when a code point that is not a [Unicode scalar value](https://www.unicode.org/glossary/#unicode_scalar_value) is encountered (optional). One of: * `'replace'`: Replace non-scalar-value with the `replacement_char`. (default) * `'ignore'`: Skip non-scalar-value . * `'strict'`: Raise an exception for any non-scalar-value.
constraints: errors must be one of replace, ignore, strict

replacement_char.description: The replacement character to be used in place of any invalid input when `errors='replace'`. Any Unicode scalar value may be used. The default value is the default Unicode replacement character which is 0xFFFD (U+65533).
constraints: replacement_char must be one of replace

output.description: A `N` dimensional `string` tensor with shape `[D1...DN]`. #### Example: >>> input = tf.ragged.constant( ... [[71, 246, 246, 100, 110, 105, 103, 104, 116], [128522]]) >>> print(unicode_encode(input, 'UTF-8')) tf.Tensor([b'G\xc3\xb6\xc3\xb6dnight' b'\xf0\x9f\x98\x8a'], shape=(2,), dtype=string)
